body:
Fixed. The cause is one step further down than the analysis here reached, and it makes most of the host-side machinery in the trace unfalsifiable.

## Root cause

`guest/agent.cmd` deleted the go flag with the mailbox **still mounted**:

```bat
del %WQ%\WQGO.TXT
...
cmd /c %WQ%\WQCMD.CMD > %WQ%\WQOUT.TXT 2> %WQ%\WQERR.TXT   :: mailbox still mounted
mountvol %WQ% /P                                            :: only flush, after the command
```

Windows synchronises a FAT volume with the underlying disk at mount and dismount and at no other time — the fact the agent's own poll loop is built on. So the delete stayed in the guest's cache until the command finished and the volume was released.

The host reads the mailbox image directly. It could not see the acknowledgement while the acknowledgement was the thing being waited for.

That makes `probe(GO).is_none()` at `runner.rs:1344` **always false** for any command still running, so the contradiction you spotted at 70.2 s / 70.3 s was not a race the workload sometimes wins — it was structural, and it applied to every command outliving the ten-second first-contact window. It also explains the second trace: `ping -n 200` sleeps between pings, moves no measurable I/O, and so trips neither `PROOF_OF_LIFE_BYTES` nor `still_moving`. Each freshly prepared guest then failed at `wait_until_gone` for the same reason, which is why the five attempts could not succeed.

## Fix

```bat
del %WQ%\WQGO.TXT >nul 2>&1
mountvol %WQ% /P >nul 2>&1        :: flush the acknowledgement to the host image
mountvol %WQ% %WQVOL% >nul 2>&1   :: take the volume back, so output has somewhere to go
```

Same round trip the poll loop already does every turn.

Measured on your reproducer, M1 / macOS 26.4 / QEMU 11.1.1:

| `winquick run --timeout 60 -- cmd /c "ping -n 200 127.0.0.1 >nul"` | |
|---|---|
| before | **182 s**, 5 discarded prepared guests, then a cold boot |
| after | **60 s**, no rebuild, prepared guest kept |

Warm `cmd /c ver` is unchanged at 310 ms p50.

## Your three suggestions

1. **Stop the retry loop early** — not taken. The cascade is gone at the root, and adding a heuristic on top of a fixed bug is exactly what produced the byte counters in the first place.
2. **Reword the two messages** — done, and the second now names a command that needs longer as the usual cause.
3. **Reconsider the 60 s threshold** — kept. You were right that 60 is the round number people reach for, but the constant was not the cause: the flag never arrived at any duration, so raising it would have moved the boundary without fixing anything. Its documentation was wrong and is corrected.

The `--help` note was right too — `--timeout` now says the clock starts when the guest takes the command.

## Why the tests missed it

`tests/integration.sh` has covered this exact shape since v0.4.1 — slow command, timeout, assertions that the prepared guest survives and the run is not retried. Both used `--timeout 2`, which is below `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_IS_CERTAIN` by construction: the range where the host declines to act on the verdict. The suite asserted the right properties at the one value for which they were free. It now runs the case at 60 s as well, a unit test asserts the agent dismounts between taking a command and starting it, and a new `tests/firstrun.sh` runs the whole thing against an install built from nothing.

For the record, this was not undiagnosed: `docs/research.md` has carried the cause and this exact one-line fix since v0.4.0 under *"the guest-side half, not shipped here"*, deferred to avoid a runtime rebuild. That note is left in place with what the deferral actually cost.

## Upgrading

The agent is baked into the image, so images built by an earlier WinQuick are stale. `winquick doctor` names each one and the command that rebuilds it — and `setup --force` alone is not enough, since the serviced images each have to be rebuilt by their own capability. Both of those were themselves wrong before this change and are fixed here.

Thanks for the report — the traces, the control runs and the pointer to `runner.rs:1344` are what made it findable.
